name: Approve Switch
description: Two equal pills — Reject and Approve — where pressing one expands it in place, floods it with its decision colour and completes its own word ("Reject" → "Rejected"), while the other collapses into an undo circle. One persistent node per slot, so the pill morphs with `layout` rather than being swapped, and the base word glides inside the widening pill instead of cross-fading. Approve throws confetti; reject gets a shake and a single impact ring, because celebrating a rejection is the wrong feeling.

variations.name: default
variations.previewHint: Press Approve for confetti or Reject for a shake and an impact ring, then hit the undo circle
variations.description: A two-pill decision control that morphs in place: the pressed slot expands and tints while the other collapses to an undo circle, the word completes itself with a dropped-in suffix, and each verdict gets its own one-shot flourish.

props.name: className
props.description: Appended to the root wrapper's classes for call-site layout overrides.

features: Keeps one persistent button per slot so `layout` can replace `layoutId` — state changes the node's size, colour and children, never its identity
Glides the base word instead of cross-fading it: "Reject" is one text node that never unmounts, and only the suffix "ed" mounts, dropping in from above
Recolours the badge in place with animated SVG fill and stroke, so the disc and glyph invert without the icon ever blinking
Splits the reward layer by verdict — confetti for approve, a shake plus a single impact ring for reject — and mounts neither under reduced motion
Hangs both flourishes off a non-animating wrapper, because an absolutely-positioned child of a `layout` element gets scaled and smeared by that element's morph

Paints every colour from a --as-* token through var(), floods the decision tone as an overlay whose opacity Motion springs, and flips the ink on a matching 240ms CSS transition — so the fills stay live against the theme

featureSections.title: One Node Per Slot
featureSections.summary: Both screens are the same two boxes changing shape, not two components fading past each other.
points: Runs `layout` on a button that is never unmounted, so Motion measures before and after and interpolates the difference
Drives size entirely from class changes — a fixed expanded width, and a collapsed width equal to the shared pill height so it lands as a circle
Keeps border-radius as an inline pixel value so Motion can undo the corner distortion the layout scale introduces
Pins the badge with layout="position" so it stays centred rather than being stretched by the parent's morph

featureSections.title: The Completing Word
featureSections.summary: The label finishes itself rather than being replaced, which is why no per-letter identity is needed.
points: Leaves the base word as a single text node that glides with its wrapper inside the widening pill
Mounts only the suffix, arriving from -0.55em through a 4px blur and leaving downward, so the past tense reads as dropping into place
Drops the whole label on the collapsing slot via popLayout, so the pill shrinks around it instead of waiting for the fade
Exits content on a 0.16s flat spring — half the arrival — so no text is ever visible outside a shrinking pill

featureSections.title: Reward Layer
featureSections.summary: Two one-shot flourishes, mounted only while a slot is expanded so they replay on every fresh decision.
points: Throws a hydration-safe confetti field seeded from a sin-based frac(index), fanned across the upper half only
Splits x and y onto separate curves so gravity lives on y alone: the throw eases out while the drop eases in
Answers a rejection with a 7-step shake on the wrapper and one boxShadow ring scaling to 1.14 and gone — impact, not applause
Shakes the wrapper rather than the button, leaving the button's own transform free for `layout` to drive

featureSections.title: Theming & Accessibility
featureSections.summary: Motion drives the shape; CSS drives the colour, so every fill stays a live token and follows a theme flip on its own.
points: Paints the resting pill from --as-pill and never changes it — the decision tone is a separate overlay laid on top, so the pill is visible at rest, before hydration, and behind every state
Springs the tone in on opacity alone: the one visual channel Motion can animate without parsing a colour, which is what lets the fill stay a var() the theme can move underneath
Publishes the slot's own tone as --as-tone on the button, so the overlay and the badge disc read it without either being handed a literal
Flips the ink — color, fill and stroke — on a 240ms CSS transition matched to the tone's spring, rather than in JS where an oklch() token cannot be parsed
Keeps the approve and reject tones identical in both themes: they are the meaning of the control, not its surface
Labels the collapsed slot "Undo decision", reflects the verdict with aria-pressed, hides both flourishes from the accessibility tree, and drops them entirely under prefers-reduced-motion
